key_insight: Update-matched unlearning shows that resisting relearning should be judged against the model after the same update, not a pre-update reference, because that better preserves plasticity while still suppressing unwanted knowledge.
engineering_relevance: For continuously adapted LLMs in safety-critical workflows, this method helps block harmful recovery of deleted behavior without unnecessarily degrading future task learning.
method: Apply the same simulated relearning update to both the defended model and an undefended reference initialized from the same unlearned model.
Use new-task learning performance to select the model, alongside relearning-resistance metrics.
Test the reference-timing hypothesis across multiple unlearning methods and base models.
evidence_signal: On TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen, UMU reduced harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while improving new-task accuracy by 3.5 points.
watch_item: Results depend on the choice of simulated update and evaluation tasks, so the approach may require careful tuning to transfer to different downstream fine-tuning settings.
paper_title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
